newsitem.title: USA: New York Power Pool members target ISO by mid-1997.
newsitem.headline: New York Power Pool members target ISO by mid-1997.

text.p: The target of New York Power Pool members discussing an independent system operator (ISO) for New York's power transmission is a mid-1997 startup.

That would be the first step of a two step process seen by the utilities, with the second coming in mid-1998, they said in a status report submitted to the New York State Public Service Commission Tuesday.

It said these dates are contingent on U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission approvals and reaching several technical milestones, in particular developing software with the group's outside vendor ABB Group.

The report said, at one point, the power pool members expect to file at FERC by December 31. This is after it said they "believe that December 31, 1996, is the earliest achievable target date for the FERC filings."

The power pool members are Central Hudson Gas & Electric Corp, Consolidated Edison Co of New York Inc, Long Island Lighting Co, Niagara Mohawk Power Corp, the New York Power Authority, New York State Electric & Gas Corp, Orange & Rockland Utilities Inc and Rochester Gas and Electric Corp.
The report said its utility members and the Power Authority expect to file a joint proposal to restructure the power pool to implement wholesale competition.
As envisioned, the structure would include revised transmission tariffs, an ISO and a power exchange.

The ISO would provide for efficient and reliable operation of the bulk power system and the power exchange would coordinate a competitive energy market within the reliability standards set by the ISO, the report explained.
It notes the term ISO frequently denotes a single entity responsible for reliability and commercial functions.

To "more accurately define the functions of our proposed entities, we are considering using the terms system security operator and independent system coordinator to denote the realiability and commercial organizations."

"We believe that the filing (proposed) exceeds in scope the requirements of FERC Order 888 for compliance filing by tight power pools," it said, refering to FERC's April order addressing open access and stranded costs.
The report said three members -- Con Edison, Lilco and the Power Authority -- also need Internal Revenue Service approval of changes in tax-exempt bond indentures.
The group said its effort has resulted in a competitive framework based on locational energy prices.

Their mid-1997 target includes an ISO and power exchange structures in place, with a competitive energy market and "open access transmission tariffs based on LBMP" -- or locational based marginal pricing.
They said the mid-1998 target is to have:
-- day-ahead unit commitment and energy market,
-- real-time security-constrained balancing market,
-- competitive capacity market, and
-- competitive ancillary services.
The report said work is still needed on:
-- procedures to implement security-constrained dispatch and unit commitment based on bid prices;
-- mechanisms for energy, capacity and ancillary service auctions by the power exchange;
-- procedures for defining the quantity of Transmission Congestion Contracts available, the financial rights available through these contracts, and how they would be allocated;
-- settlement procedures for a day-ahead market; and
-- structure of the ISO and power exchange.

It said the group will also have to review the restructuring filings made by members in the past week as the treatment of corporate structure and load pocket mitigation will be relevant to the group's FERC filing.
